deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, 1983-84): Grothendieck is building a combinatorial theory of 'systèmes de pseudo-droites'. X is a surface, essentially the real projective plane or a piece of it. K is a family of pseudo-lines; L appears to be a second system, and K∪L is considered. The cell complex (X,K) has faces F. The previous page set up 'lois de symétrisation' around exceptional and ordinary edges, with multiplicities ν(s), indices ν(a), and types II_p of Σ. The next page gives the explicit recipe for inserting the new order-2 vertices.

This page, dated 7.2.1984, axiomatizes the resulting structure on K.
(1) The old vertices of K are the crossings, of order 4. K is refined to a topological graph by adding new vertices of order 2. The set S_K of new vertices splits as a disjoint union S'_K ⊔ S''_K, red and black vertices respectively. From the next page, red vertices seem to be the points of K∩L on the edges.
(2) Axiom a): for every face F, the red and black vertices on ∂F give a subdivision of the boundary polygon ∂F. Two consecutive vertices on ∂F are never both of order 4. More precisely, on every 'big edge' joining two consecutive crossings there is at least one red vertex and at least one black vertex. The number of red vertices is specified except in type II_p or on an exceptional edge.
(3) Axiom b): a 'déplacement' K' of K, i.e. a push-off or parallel copy, gives each edge a of each face F a sign ε_F(a) = ±1, according to whether the push-off goes into F or not. This is a co-orientation of the curves, written as signs on flags (face, edge). The rules are:
  - ε_{F'}(a) = −ε_F(a) for the two faces on either side of a.
  - ε_F(a) = ε_F(b) when a and b meet on ∂F at an order-2 vertex, so the sign is constant along a big edge.
  - ε_{F1}(a1) = ε_{F2}(a2) when F1 and F2 share an edge b ending at a crossing s, and a1, a2 ≠ b are the other edges of F1, F2 at s. This works because a1 and a2 lie on the same pseudo-line through s, and F1, F2 are on the same side of it.
(4) Consequence claimed: every face is a polygon with 4n sides in the refined graph. For each edge a, there is a 'symmetry' σ_a = σ_a^F : Pol(F) → Pol(F') of the boundary polygons of the two adjacent faces. It is characterized as the polygon isomorphism fixing both endpoints of a, and σ_a^F σ_a^{F'} = id. It fixes every vertex and edge on the big edge â containing a, but not the neighbouring vertices beyond the bounding crossings. It exchanges red and black vertices.

Purpose: to give each face a combinatorial regular-polygon structure, with edge-reflections compatible across adjacent faces. This is a step toward rebuilding the arrangement (Σ) from purely numerical and combinatorial data on K (item n of the previous page), and probably toward a canonical symmetric or geometric model of the arrangement.
errors: The deduction 'all faces are 4n-gons' is asserted but not justified on the page. Axiom a) only gives at least one red and one black vertex per big edge, with an exact count only outside type II_p and exceptional edges. A 4n count needs a precise parity or alternation rule that is not stated here.
Notation slip: the third sign rule is written ε_{a1}(F1) = ε_{a2}(F2), with indices inverted relative to the earlier notation ε_F(a).

σ_a is said to be characterized by fixing the two endpoints of a. A polygon isomorphism Pol(F) → Pol(F') fixing an edge is determined only once the polygons have the same number of sides. The page also has σ_a both fixing all of the big edge â and swapping red and black vertices. That is consistent only if â carries a colour-symmetric pattern, or if 'fixed' means fixed as positions with colours exchanged. The page leaves this unclear.

ideas.what: Refining a pseudo-line arrangement graph by two-coloured order-2 vertices (red = intersections with an auxiliary system L, black = midpoints/other) so every face boundary becomes a coloured subdivided polygon
ideas.modern_name: Barycentric-type subdivision / coloured map refinement of an arrangement (cf. bipartite maps, flag complexes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in combinatorial topology; arrangements: Levi (1926), Ringel, Grünbaum, Goodman–Pollack
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses maps/dessins and alludes to work on real/tame geometry; no published detailed treatment of pseudo-line systems known to me

ideas.what: Signs ε_F(a) from a push-off K' of K, with sign rules across edges, order-2 vertices and crossings
ideas.modern_name: Co-orientation of pseudo-lines; local side data, akin to sign vectors / covectors of the oriented matroid

ideas.what: Edge-reflections σ_a: Pol(F) → Pol(F') between adjacent face polygons, involutive and colour-swapping, fixing the big edge
ideas.modern_name: Reflection (Coxeter-like/flag) structure on a map; a combinatorial 'regular polygon' gluing
ideas.usually_credited_to: Flag-graph / reflection descriptions of maps (Coxeter; Jones–Singerman 1978 for maps)
ideas.where_published: Analogous ideas on canonical regular realisations of maps appear in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §3 (regular polyhedra)

missed.claim: Grothendieck equips the cells of a pseudo-line arrangement with a two-coloured subdivision (faces are 4n-gons) and involutive, colour-swapping edge reflections between adjacent faces. This is the kind of structure that would give each arrangement a canonical symmetric or geometric realization: faces as regular 4n-gons glued by reflections. It parallels the canonical regular-polyhedron and Belyi-type realizations of maps he describes in the Esquisse, written in the same months. This bridge between pseudo-line or oriented-matroid combinatorics and his dessin/reflection-group programme does not seem to have been developed in the literature.
missed.quote: on a une ... de symétrie autour de a ... σ_a : Pol(F) ⥲ Pol(F') caractérisé par la condition qu'il laisse fixes les deux extrémités de a ... transforme sommets rouges (resp. noirs) en sommets noirs
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Canonical geometric representatives of pseudo-line arrangements (realizability, 'stretchability' alternatives via piecewise-regular metrics) remain of interest. A map-theoretic and dessin viewpoint on arrangements could link oriented-matroid theory with the Esquisse programme. The thread is only sketched here.

missed.claim: The programme of reconstructing the arrangement Σ from the coloured graph K plus numerical data (vertex orders ν(s), edge indices ν(a), symmetrization laws) is stated but not completed on this page. The 4n-gon claim is left unproved.
missed.quote: Il résulte des faits que toutes les faces sont des [polygones d']ordre 4n
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A combinatorial encoding theorem of this type would be a Grothendieck-style classification of arrangements. Its status in the remaining pages of cote 154 is unknown.

deep.surprise_reason: This is mostly routine combinatorial-topological bookkeeping: colouring subdivision vertices, co-orientation signs, and the polygon isomorphism across an edge. The mildly notable point is the systematic edge-reflection structure on an arrangement of pseudo-lines, apparently aimed at a canonical symmetric model. It resonates with the Esquisse but is unpublished and only sketched.
transcription_corrections: Line 1–2: likely 'Structure de K. Les sommets [nouveaux] sont des sommets d'ordre 2, soit S_K l'ensemble des sommets' — 'l'un des' should be 'l'ensemble des'.
'On désigne par K le graphe hyp.' should read 'le graphe top[ologique]', followed by '[avec] ses nouveaux sommets (les anciens sont ceux d'ordre 4)'.
'toutes les faces sont des ... ordre 4n' is probably 'sont des polygones d'ordre 4n'; 'Il résulte des faits que' is probably 'Il résulte de ce fait que'.
Third sign rule: written ε_{a1}(F1) = ε_{a2}(F2) in the manuscript; it means ε_{F1}(a1) = ε_{F2}(a2).
'signe ε_F(a), qui est ±1 si ...' should probably read '+1 si le [déplacement] est dirigé vers l'intérieur de F, −1 sinon'.
The NB under the S_K decomposition is uncertain. 'pris sur des sommets d'ordre 4' is probably not correct; the next page suggests red vertices are the points of K∩L on the edges.
